regime.whatWouldChangeMind: Canonical MOVE rise, sustained IG OAS widening or persistent intraday Fed‑funds‑futures repricing across 5m–4h would show transmission into broader risk‑off and invalidate the selective‑stress view.

stories.title: AI suppliers report large capex and strong margins even as some AI names dip.
stories.whatChanged: Issuer disclosures (TSMC, CoreWeave) show sizable revenue/margins and large capex/capitalised software spending.
stories.whyItMatters: Strong supplier fundamentals support AI infrastructure demand and can sustain sector leadership despite episodic equity weakness.
stories.mechanism: Sustained demand for AI compute drives supplier revenue and justifies capex; short‑term equity dips may reflect sentiment or positioning, not necessarily end‑demand collapse.
stories.conclusion: Issuer-level results support continued AI infrastructure demand and capex absorption; selective equity weakness alone does not prove a demand shock.
stories.whatWouldChangeMind: Confirmed issuer downgrades to revenue/cash‑flow or matched canonical priced reactions (sustained share-price falls tied to company guidance) would overturn this conclusion.

stories.title: High‑yield spreads have widened sharply while IG barely moved — selective credit stress, not systemic yet.
stories.whatChanged: 20‑session HY OAS widened ~53bp to 2026‑10‑15 while IG OAS rose only ~6bp over the same window.
stories.whyItMatters: A HY‑focused widening can signal issuer/sector stress or positioning-driven re‑pricing; systemic credit contagion requires concurrent IG and MOVE weakness.
stories.mechanism: Either issuer‑level risks and sector repricing hit HY, or rising real yields and funding costs selectively press weaker credit; broader transmission would show up in IG and volatility measures.
stories.conclusion: Credit stress currently appears concentrated in HY; evidence does not yet show broad IG contagion or volatility‑led systemic risk.
stories.whatWouldChangeMind: Sustained IG OAS widening, a rising MOVE index, or correlated breadth deterioration beyond AI names would indicate transmission to systemic credit risk.

stories.title: Nominal yields remain high but model term premium fell; long‑end pressure looks concentrated in real yields.
stories.whatChanged: US 10Y nominal ~5.09% and NY Fed ACM 10Y term premium estimate fell to ~0.75% (5‑session -23.7bp).
stories.whyItMatters: A falling model term premium with high nominal yields implies long‑end moves are driven more by real‑rate increases than persistent term‑premium repricing — affects policy/risk outlook and auction/flow vulnerability.
stories.mechanism: Real yields rise (growth/real‑rate channel) while model term premium contracts; separate auction/flow or dealer‑structure mechanisms remain possible but unproven.
stories.conclusion: Current diagnostics point to a real‑yield‑driven long‑end rather than a sustained term‑premium regime; outstanding volatility and auction/flow evidence are needed to confirm.
stories.whatWouldChangeMind: Canonical MOVE/Treasury volatility data, dealer stress rules, or auction when‑issued tails showing persistent absorption issues would shift the conclusion toward a term‑premium or structural‑demand story.

verified.title: Long-end Treasury stress
verified.detail: On 24 September 2026, the U.S. Treasury par yield curve closed with the 10-year yield at 5.18% and the 30-year yield at 5.47%, confirming severe long-duration rate pressure.

verified.title: S&P concentration remains extreme
verified.detail: Nvidia and Apple together accounted for more than 15% of the S&P 500, reinforcing the concentration risk behind an index that can remain firm even when participation is weaker.

verified.title: Saudi/Houthi energy risk persists
verified.detail: Saudi-led coalition forces said six Houthi ballistic missiles were intercepted on 24 September, with Yanbu among the targeted areas; the report also described claimed attacks on Saudi Aramco facilities in Yanbu.

verified.title: Duration stress is global
verified.detail: A Bloomberg global sovereign-bond yield gauge approached 4%, the highest level since 2007, supporting the view that duration pressure is global rather than solely a U.S. Treasury story.

verified.title: Natural-gas storage tightened
verified.detail: EIA reported Lower-48 working gas at 3,351 Bcf for the week ended 18 September 2026, a 53 Bcf weekly injection and 95 Bcf above the five-year average.

verified.title: NBIS analyst catalyst verified
verified.detail: BNP Paribas upgraded Nebius Group from Neutral to Outperform and raised its price target from $260 to $399 on 24 September 2026, independently confirming a catalyst cited in the StockedUp transcript.

verified.title: US–China tariff cliff pushed out
verified.detail: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the U.S. and China agreed to extend their trade truce through 10 January 2027, reducing the immediate tariff-cliff risk while broader negotiations continue.

verified.title: US–Iran diplomacy is active
verified.detail: President Trump said U.S.-Iran talks were continuing during the UN General Assembly and that he believed a settlement would be reached; this verifies active diplomacy but not the transcript's specific Hormuz-for-sanctions terms.

verified.title: Diesel export-policy risk
verified.detail: The U.S. Chamber warned that restricting U.S. diesel or fuel exports could squeeze refiners and risk reducing supplies of diesel, gasoline and jet fuel, potentially worsening consumer costs.

verified.title: Late-September midterm seasonality
verified.detail: Citadel Securities' historical midterm-year path shows equities tending to weaken into around September 30 before a stronger average year-end phase; this supports late-September seasonality as context, not a forecast.

verified.title: META Muse catalyst verified
verified.detail: Meta launched its Muse personal AI agent and said it planned integration with smart glasses, independently confirming the product catalyst behind the creator's META discussion.

verified.title: RKLB defence-space catalyst verified
verified.detail: Rocket Lab said it was selected for the U.S. Space Force NITE-STAR IDIQ program, which has a ceiling of up to $981 million across participating vendors, confirming the defence-space catalyst cited by StockedUp.
